name: Deny by default
summary: Nothing is allowed until a rule allows it.
description: Denies every request. Start here and insert or write the rules that allow what you need. Assigned appliance-wide, it also decides public discovery reads such as /discovery and /.well-known/ucp.
rules: default allow := false

docs.label: Concept: default allow vs default deny

name: Require authenticated caller
summary: Allow only callers that authenticated.
description: Allows a request only when the caller authenticated with one of the surface's Caller Context methods. Denies callers whose credential was missing or invalid, and requests on a surface without caller authentication.

name: Allow by JWT claim or role
summary: Allow only JWT callers whose claim has one of the listed values.
description: Allows a request when the caller authenticated with a JWT and the chosen claim, such as role, holds one of the listed values. A claim that is a list matches when any of its values is listed. Denies every other caller.

parameters.label: Claim
parameters.help: The JWT claim to check, for example role, roles or groups.

parameters.label: Allowed values
parameters.help: Separate values with commas.

docs.label: Guide: Use JWT claims to control access

name: Allow by JWT issuer and audience
summary: Allow only tokens from listed issuers for listed audiences.
description: Allows a request only when the caller's JWT was issued by one of the listed issuers and names one of the listed audiences. Denies every other caller. A token without an aud claim, as from an identity provider whose JWT Bearer method checks client_id or azp instead, is denied.

parameters.label: Allowed issuers
parameters.help: Exact iss values, separated by commas.

parameters.label: Allowed audiences
parameters.help: Exact aud values, separated by commas.

name: Restrict MCP tools by role
summary: Admins call any tool; other callers only the safe tools.
description: Allows callers whose JWT role claim, a single value or a list, holds an admin role to call any MCP tool, other authenticated callers to call only the listed safe tools, and authenticated callers to use other MCP methods such as tools/list. Denies a request without input.mcp, such as a JSON-RPC message without an id. A caller is authenticated when it passed one of the surface's Caller Context methods, such as JWT Bearer or API Key. Use it as the whole policy: inserted into another policy it would allow requests that policy denies.

parameters.label: Admin roles
parameters.help: Values of the JWT role claim that may call any tool, separated by commas. A role claim that is a list matches when any of its values is listed.

parameters.label: Safe tools
parameters.help: MCP tools every authenticated caller may call, separated by commas.

examples.name: Roles list with admin calls any tool
API key caller lists the tools
API key caller calls another tool
Id-less tools/call from an API key caller

docs.label: Concept: restrict tool access by role

name: Require Trust Registry recognition
summary: Allow only agents the Trust Registry recognises.
description: Allows a request only when the calling agent's DID is verified as the caller's identity and the Trust Registry recognised it. A DID is verified when it is the caller identity the gateway established (input.agent.did_verified), not only a DID the request names. Needs Extract Trust Registry Data on the surface; without it input.agent is absent and every request is denied.

name: Require verified credential subject
summary: Allow only listed caller DIDs the gateway verified.
description: Allows a request only when the gateway verified the caller's DID, from an identity presentation or a bound source credential, and that DID is on the list. Denies unverified and unlisted callers.

parameters.label: Allowed DIDs
parameters.help: Caller DIDs, separated by commas.

name: Allowlist outbound destinations
summary: Allow Transit Point calls only to the listed destinations.
description: Allows a request through a Transit Point only when the Transit Point's configured endpoint (input.gateway.target_id) is one of the listed destinations or a path under one. It decides as a Transit Point policy or the shared Transit Point policy, where input.gateway.direction is outbound; as the surface's Access Point or Target policy it allows every request. Use it as the whole policy: inserted into another policy it would allow requests that policy denies.

parameters.label: Allowed destinations
parameters.help: Separate destinations with commas: an endpoint URL such as https://api.example.com, or fabric://<gateway id> for a Fabric route. A Transit Point matches when its endpoint is a listed destination or a path under it, never a longer host name.

examples.name: Transit Point to a listed endpoint
Transit Point to a path under a listed endpoint
Transit Point to a host that starts with a listed one
Transit Point to a longer host name
Fabric route to a listed gateway

name: Business-hours access window
summary: Allow or deny requests by time of day, day of week and time zone.
description: Allows, or denies, requests made inside a daily time window on the listed days, in the chosen time zone; requests outside the window get the opposite decision. A window whose end is earlier than its start crosses midnight, and each listed day gets the hours after midnight and the hours before it on that day's own date. Rate limits are set on the surface's Rate Limit panel, not in policy.

parameters.label: Inside the window
parameters.help: Allow lets requests through only inside the window. Deny refuses requests inside the window and lets every other request through.

parameters.label: Days
parameters.help: English day names, separated by commas. Leave empty for every day. A day is the request's date in the time zone below.

parameters.label: From
parameters.help: Start of the window, as HH:MM.

parameters.label: Until
parameters.help: End of the window, as HH:MM; requests from this time on are outside it. A time earlier than From makes the window cross midnight, for example 22:00 to 06:00. Each part counts on its own date: with Days Monday to Friday, 22:00 to 06:00 covers 00:00 to 06:00 and 22:00 to midnight on Monday to Friday, so Monday 01:00 is inside and Saturday 01:00 is outside.

parameters.label: Time zone
parameters.help: An IANA time zone, for example Europe/Berlin or Asia/Singapore.

name: All trust checks pass
summary: Allow only if every target trust check passed.
description: Allows a request only if at least one Trust Check ran on the target leg (input.trust_check_results.target: the Managed Agent's Target, or the Transit Point the request goes through) and every one passed. A check that queries several authorities passes when any of them recognises the entity. Denies when any check failed or none ran. Trust Checks on the Access Point are not read.

name: At least N trust checks pass
summary: Threshold instead of all-or-nothing. Has a setting.
description: Allows a request when the number of Trust Checks that passed on the target leg (input.trust_check_results.target: the Managed Agent's Target, or the Transit Point the request goes through) reaches your threshold. A check that queries several authorities counts once, and passes when any of them recognises the entity. Denies when fewer pass, or when no checks ran. Trust Checks on the Access Point are not counted.

parameters.label: Minimum passing checks
parameters.help: Updates the Rego below. You can still edit the code after using the template.

examples.name: 2 checks, each with 1 of 2 authorities recognising

name: Allow listed HTTP methods
summary: Allow only the listed HTTP methods.
description: Allows a request only when its HTTP method is on the list, for example to keep a surface read-only. Assigned appliance-wide, it also decides public discovery reads such as /discovery and /.well-known/ucp.
rules:
default allow := false

allow if input.http.method in {{methods}}

parameters.label: Allowed methods
parameters.help: Upper case, separated by commas.

name: Allow listed paths
summary: Allow only requests under the listed path prefixes.
description: Allows a request only when its path starts with one of the listed prefixes. Denies a path that contains .., %2e, a backslash or %5c. Assigned appliance-wide, it also decides public discovery reads such as /discovery and /.well-known/ucp.

parameters.label: Allowed path prefixes
parameters.help: Separate prefixes with commas.

name: Allow listed surfaces
summary: Allow only requests to the listed surfaces.
description: Allows a request only when it is for one of the listed surfaces, by surface ID. Useful for a policy enforced across every surface. Assigned appliance-wide, it also decides public discovery reads such as /discovery and /.well-known/ucp.
rules:
default allow := false

allow if input.channel.config_id in {{surfaces}}

parameters.label: Surface IDs
parameters.help: Each surface's ID, shown in the read-only Surface ID field of the Surface Builder's surface panel and at the end of the surface page's address (/surfaces/<id>), separated by commas.

examples.name: Other surface with the same name

name: Allow listed subjects
summary: Allow only the listed JWT callers, by principal.
description: Allows a request only when the caller authenticated with a JWT and its subject is on the list. The subject is the value of the principal claim the JWT verification strategy names, sub unless the strategy names another. Denies every other caller.

parameters.label: Allowed subjects
parameters.help: Values of the strategy's principal claim, separated by commas.

name: Monitor-only baseline
summary: Lets everything through. For observing traffic only.
description: Allows every request, so you can watch traffic before writing a stricter policy: through the Audit Log when policy decisions are audited, or through policy input capture. To try a stricter policy without blocking, use the Monitor option of global enforcement on the Policies list instead.
rules: default allow := true

docs.label: Concept: default allow vs default deny

name: Tool policy: allow authenticated callers
summary: For a tool binding: allow any caller with a token.
description: For a policy bound to MCP tools, which decides each tools/call to the surface's MCP Target: allows a call when the request's bearer token has a sub claim. It reads the claims of the bearer token in the request's Authorization header (input.jwt), so use it on a surface whose Caller Context authenticates that header with JWT Bearer.
rules:
default allow := false

allow if input.jwt.sub

name: Tool policy: allow by JWT claim
summary: For a tool binding: allow callers whose claim has a listed value.
description: For a policy bound to MCP tools, which decides each tools/call to the surface's MCP Target: allows a call when a claim of the request's bearer token, a single value or a list, has one of the listed values. Covers admin-only and subscription-based access. It reads the claims of the bearer token in the request's Authorization header (input.jwt), so use it on a surface whose Caller Context authenticates that header with JWT Bearer.

parameters.label: Claim
parameters.help: The token claim to read, for example role or subscription.

parameters.label: Allowed values
parameters.help: Values of the claim, separated by commas.

name: Tool policy: admin role with a deny reason
summary: For a tool binding: allow one role and record why others were denied.
description: For a policy bound to MCP tools, which decides each tools/call to the surface's MCP Target: allows callers whose bearer token has the admin role and sets deny_reason when the token has no role or another role. The reason is written to the audit log only, not the response. It reads the claims of the bearer token in the request's Authorization header (input.jwt), so use it on a surface whose Caller Context authenticates that header with JWT Bearer.

parameters.label: Allowed role
parameters.help: The role claim value that may call the tool.

name: Tool policy: allow every caller
summary: For a tool binding: the tool entry list is the only control.
description: For a policy bound to MCP tools, which decides each tools/call to the surface's MCP Target: allows every call, so only the tools listed on the binding decide what can be called.
rules: default allow := true
